question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사절 안에서 선행사 an attachment와 수동의 관계를 이루며, 괄호 안의 의미상 주어인 애착(attachment)은 예술품 속에서 '보여지는(수동)' 대상이므로 과거분사 shown은 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 시간을 나타내는 부사구 During World War II와 함께 쓰여 과거의 역사적인 사실을 기술하는 문장으로, 정동사 과거형 became은 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): Houser's designs가 분사의 의미상 주어이며, 디자인이 전통에 '뿌리를 내리고 있는(수동적 근원)' 관계이므로 be동사 are 뒤에서 형용사구처럼 쓰인 과거분사 rooted는 어법상 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 정답인 (B)가 포함된 문장의 관계절 내부 골격은 'he(주어) + worked(동사) + as a freelance artist(부사구)'로 구성되어 있어 빠진 명사 성분이 없는 완전한 절입니다. 관계대명사 which는 뒤에 주어나 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끌어야 하므로, 여기서는 장소의 선행사 Santa Fe를 수식하면서 부사 역할을 대신할 수 있는 관계부사 where(혹은 전치사+관계대명사 형태인 in which)가 들어가야 어법상 옳은 문장이 됩니다. 따라서 which를 where로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계부사 vs 관계대명사 — 뒤이어 나오는 절의 완전성 여부로 판단
(A) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 수식받는 명사(attachment)와의 수동 관계 확인
(D) 분사의 태 — 주어(Houser's designs)가 주체적으로 뿌리를 내리게 된 수동의 상태 상태 조건 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is __(A) shown__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) which__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he __(C) became__ interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(D) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless of__ his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사 other people을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로, 복수 명사를 선행사로 삼아 뒤에 복수 동사 are가 이어지므로 'who'는 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 지각동사 see의 목적격보어 자리에 있는 과거분사 immersed를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 'similarly'는 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 관계절 내의 주어인 'everybody'는 단수 취급하므로 단수 동사인 'takes'는 어법상 수 일치가 올바르게 이루어졌습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 명사구 'a wonderful way'를 수식하여 형용사적 용법으로 쓰인 부정사구이므로 'to share'는 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (A) "suffered"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "suffering"로 고쳐야 한다. 문장의 주어 we와 동사 suffer의 관계를 파악해야 합니다. suffering은 '~으로 고통받다'라는 의미를 지닌 자동사구 'suffer from'의 현재분사 진행형으로 쓰인 것으로, 주어인 we가 직접 외로움으로 고통을 겪고 있는 능동의 상태를 기술합니다. 따라서 수동태의 형태인 'suffered'로 쓰면 의미 전달이 불가능할 뿐만 아니라 문장 구조상 비문이 됩니다. 능동형인 suffering으로 고쳐 써야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (A) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 주어와 동사의 행위 관계가 능동인지 수동인지에 따라 판정
(C) 형용사 vs 부사 — 분사/형용사를 수식할 때는 부사를 사용해야 함에 착안
(D) 주어와 동사의 수 일치 — 부정대명사(everybody)의 단수 취급 원칙 적용
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are __(A) suffered__ from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else __(C) similarly__ immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody __(D) takes__ turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way __(E) to share__ an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 동사 tend는 명사나 대명사 대신 to부정사를 목적어로 취하는 성향이 있으므로, 'tend to think'는 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): If절의 주어 핵은 'a thousand lines of letters'가 하나의 기술적 단위나 코드의 한 묶음을 나타내는 단수 개념으로 취급되고 있으며, 문맥상 'UNIX' 또는 'a thousand lines' 전체를 단수의 개념적 묶음으로 받아 단수 동사인 'qualifies'를 쓴 것은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 대명사 'something useful'을 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사구로, 무언가(something)가 인간의 정신에 의해 '만들어지는' 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 'produced'는 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'responsible for ~'가 이끄는 형용사구로, 앞에 있는 명사 'the multiple overlapping technologies'를 뒤에서 수식하고 있으므로 형용사 'responsible'은 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (E) "than"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "as"로 고쳐야 한다. 원문에서는 'as much an invention as...' 구문이 사용되어 동등 비교(원급 비교)를 나타내고 있습니다. 앞에 동등 비교를 나타내는 부사 'as'가 사용되었으므로, 뒷부분의 비교 대상 앞에는 비교급과 호응하는 'than'이 아니라 원급 비교의 짝인 접속사 'as'를 써야 어법상 완전히 일치합니다. 따라서 'than'을 'as'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 학생들은 'much'라는 단어의 존재만 보고 성급하게 비교급 구문으로 착각하여 'than'을 맞는 표현으로 오판하기 쉽습니다.
keyPoints: (E) 비교구문 — 원급 비교 부사 as와 호응하는 비교 대상 접속사 as의 선택
(B) 수일치 — 주어 구절의 수 정보 판정 및 동사 형태 결정
(C) 분사의 능수동 — 명사를 수식하는 분사의 의미상 주어와의 수동 관계 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend __(A) to think__ of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(B) qualifies__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(D) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is __(E) than__ much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The human brain is wired to look for threats

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime).

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'be wired to-v'는 '~하도록 타고나다, 설정되다'라는 수동태 표현으로서, 인간의 뇌가 위협을 찾도록 설정되어 작동한다는 의미이므로 과거분사 wired는 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 괄호 안의 관계절에서 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사 which가 앞선 절 내용 전체를 선행사로 받으므로, 단수 동사 explains를 쓴 구조는 정동사 자리에 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 타동사구 write down의 목적어절을 이끌면서 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 연결하고 선행사가 없으므로, 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 전치사 by 뒤에 동명사가 목적어로 와서 '~함으로써'라는 수단을 나타내므로, 동명사 형태인 sharing은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 명사구 'a trait'를 선행사로 삼아 수식하는 두 개의 관계대명사절이 등위접속사 but에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있습니다. 첫 번째 관계절인 'that kept us alive...'와 병렬을 이루어 선행사 a trait를 꾸며야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 들어갈 자리입니다. 따라서 선행사를 내포하는 관계대명사 'what can prevent'는 올 수 없으며, 주격 관계대명사인 'that can prevent'로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계대명사의 병렬 구조 — 선행사가 존재할 때 관계대명사 what의 중복 제한
(C) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 관계대명사절 안의 동사 자리 판단
(D) 관계대명사 what의 조건 — 선행사가 없고 뒤 문장이 불완전할 때 명사절 유도
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is __(A) wired__ to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but __(B) what can prevent__ happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which __(C) explains__ why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down __(D) what went__ well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by __(E) sharing__ a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education

markedExpressions.label: (B)

markedExpressions.label: (C)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사 'shapes, colors, and concepts'를 수식하며, 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절('we have learned ~')을 이끌고 있으므로 목적격 관계대명사 'that'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'rather than' 뒤에서 앞서 언급된 'storing information'과 대조를 이루며 병렬 구조로 동명사 'storing'이 쓰였으므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 문장의 주어 핵이 복수 명사인 'People'이며, 'who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail'이라는 긴 관계사절의 수식을 받고 있습니다. 따라서 복수 동사 'struggle'은 수일치상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 'The discovery'에 연결되는 본동사 자리입니다. 주 격 관계절이나 동격절('that our memories ~ like a movie')을 건너뛰고 문장 전체의 서술어 역할을 하는 과거시제 정동사 'undermined'가 쓰였으므로 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 주어는 동명사구인 'representing the world as abstract ideas and features'입니다. 영어 문장에는 반드시 하나의 정동사(본동사)가 존재해야 하므로, 이 동명사 주어에 연결되는 술어 동사 자리에 준동사인 'coming'이 오면 정동사가 없는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 'coming'을 단수 선행 명사구(동명사구 주어)에 수일치되면서 과거 혹은 현재의 시제를 표현할 수 있는 정동사인 'comes'로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정·준동사 — 본동사 자리에 준동사 중복 사용 여부 판정
(C) 수일치 — 관계사절의 수식을 받는 복수 주어 명사 'People'과의 수일치

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."
